notes.title: Early Access v0.5.5 Hotfix / Upcoming Update Plans
notes.notes:
Bug fixes
Fixed an issue in multiplayer where players could join an already-deployed session and the game would become unplayable.

Fixed a bug in multiplayer where non-host players could launch into the world from the lobby.


Known issues
Thank you very much to everyone who has been playing since the start of Early Access.

To address the currently confirmed issues, we plan to release a hotfix sometime next week.


We are prioritizing fixes for the following frequently reported points:



UI / UX: We will improve the automatic text advance in dialogue speech bubbles in the October update.

Multiplayer / Network: We are sequentially addressing connection instability and behavior in random matchmaking.

  *Note: for random matchmaking we are also considering a fundamental overhaul as part of the large December update.*



We will publish full hotfix details in the patch notes when the update is released. We’ll continue improving the game with reference to your feedback — thank you for your continued support.



Other known issues (selected)

Backgrounds may not display correctly when zooming the screen in/out.

In Goddess' Game, if Oath Level is 1 or higher and Summon Strong Foe is enabled, reward items may fail to drop.

Some languages contain incorrect translations.

Some screens may not respond correctly when using a controller.

We have confirmed an issue where, if you exit via Suspend Save, then join multiplayer and switch to another player character, the character from the resumed suspend save can change.



Issues already listed in the v0.5.2 release notes (reposted here for reference)

Player desyncs in multiplayer.

After switch selection, some players’ doors may not open, blocking progress.

In certain multiplayer cutscenes, other players’ animations may not display correctly.

Altar text may overflow in some languages.

Missing characters / glyphs in some languages.

Player enhancement descriptions for From the Brink and Never Surrender differ from their actual effects.

The display for the Healing Spring may be incorrect in-world.

Barrier values may not carry over when resuming from a Suspend Save.

If time runs out while the Ratakaruta selection screen is open, the selection screen may remain after phase transition.

Damage/heal calculations that include decimals may be incorrectly truncated, causing small result deviations.

Critical checks for multi-hit attacks are currently evaluated per action rather than per hit.

Chain Lightning’s Ratatability and Decorune damage buff do not activate for enemies other than the directly hit target.

Facility unlock demos may not display correctly when returning to Rataport.

Certain Crow lines may not display.

Resuming from Suspend Save may be counted as an extra deployment.

Boss defeat SE may play unexpectedly upon resuming from Suspend Save.

When acquiring Ratakaruta after resuming, “Swap” may incorrectly display as “Obtain.”

Some popup help screens still show old-version in-game assets.

Incorrect description text for Magical Cobun’s hustle skill Gravity Wand in some language builds.

Element Force Ratakaruta effect text may display incorrectly.

Repeated fast operations in the Crafting screen may temporarily lower performance.

Bottom-of-screen control guides may overlap with guides from other screens.

Ratakaruta ownership info may not display when obtaining them at an Altar.

After resuming from Suspend Save, items and shop inventories in intervals may change.

Bombardier Cobun’s squad skill Rolling Bomb may exhibit unintended behavior when colliding with the Goodie Gate.

If Max HP Up is obtained while a barrier is active, barrier amount may increase.

Markers at boss attack impact points may sometimes remain visible after impact.

notes.title: Early Access v0.5.2 Release Notes
notes.notes:
Highlight
All Ratatan have been unlocked.

You can now freely assemble your unique companions, greatly expanding your tactical options.

All weapon types have been unlocked.

All weapons, including Bombs, Wands, Hammers, and Sickle, are now available. With explosions, magic, heavy strikes, and other unique actions, you can tackle challenges in diverse ways.

New worlds have been unlocked.

World 3: Jam Jammer Jungle Journey is now available.

A dense jungle area awaits, with guardians of ancient ruins like the Rock’n’Golem and giant plant monsters such as Rafflison.

World 4: Frozen Flower Fantasia is now available.

Set in a kingdom of flowers trapped in eternal winter, this stage features icy enemies such as Chillwarden, master of the great ice mirror, and Thawner, the princess’s royal guard bound by a curse of ice.

World 5: Bonedead Theatre is now available.

Set in a grand stone theater where cheerful ghosts reside, this stage pits you against foes like the broken teddy bear Boneless Bear and the theater’s superstar Flipflop. A unique stage blending horror with showtime flair.

A new system, The Goddess Games, has been added.

This is endgame content, available after clearing World 5.

You can make vows to adjust the difficulty yourself and, in return, obtain weapon limit-break materials.

By choosing to summon foes, bosses in each world will take on even more powerful forms.

Altars have been implemented.

Placed within each world, these allow you to spend costs in exchange for various rewards.

Main effects include:

Goddess Original: Obtain a random Ratakaruta

Goddess Lottery: Obtain a random weapon

Goddess Lucky Draw: The next Ratakaruta you obtain is guaranteed to be Legendary

Mega Goddess Lottery: A superior version of Goddess Lottery

Mega Goddess Original: A superior version of Goddess Original

Ratakaruta have been significantly updated.

New effects have been added, and the stats and appearance rates of existing cards have been adjusted. High-rarity cards now drop more frequently, further widening tactical options.

Card effect descriptions have also been revised to better reflect their actual behavior, making them clearer.

Base features have been expanded.

New upgrade options have been added to the Ratatan Dock, allowing progression-based growth.

The Support Desk has new support options, expanding meta-enhancement choices.

The Quest Board now features Ratatan-specific quests. Clearing them during adventures rewards you with weapons, minions, and more.

Suspend Save is now supported.

You can now interrupt your adventure mid-progress and resume later.

No need to complete long sessions in one go—you can enjoy the game with peace of mind.

When resuming, play will restart after an INTERVAL phase.

Tutorials have been greatly updated.

A new Help function has been added to clearly guide players through systems and controls.

“Crow’s Advice” has been introduced, giving you practical hints during play.

You can now choose to display HP/MP at the bottom of the screen (or keep them at the top, as before).

A new TIPS function has been added, showing helpful info during loading screens.

UI and text across the game have been refined for more natural, easy-to-understand localization.


[hr][/hr]

Battle
Adjustments have been made to each cobun type:

Soldier Cobun: Expanded upward field of vision, making it easier to handle flying enemies. Adjusted movement correction based on Intelligence to improve overall behavior balance.

Pike Cobun: Enlarged hit collision to make attacks easier to land. Adjusted attack angles to improve accuracy.

Ranger Cobun: Reduced the gap between the landing points of the first and second normal attacks. Improved targeting for Torrential Arrow and Toxic Arrow, making them easier to hit.

Bombardier Cobun: Increased power of normal attacks and shortened detonation time. Normal attacks and Roman Candle now land properly on aerial platforms. Roman Candle is now fixed at 3 shots, with increased power per shot. Targeting has been adjusted to make hits on bosses easier.

Assault Cobun: Enlarged hit collision for normal attacks. Knockback direction now aligns with the attack direction.

Magical Cobun: Adjusted movement correction based on Intelligence. Adjusted duration of Hustle Tech and improved visual clarity of effects. Adjusted angle, number, and power of fire-element meteor projectiles. Changed hit intervals for water/ice/poison projectiles, making ricochets easier to follow in large boss fights. Adjusted upward field of vision and power for stationary lightning/wind attacks.

Ninja Cobun: Adjusted movement correction based on Intelligence.

Mauler Cobun: Adjusted movement correction based on Intelligence.

Mimizukkyun’s equippable weapon types have been changed.

Equippable weapons changed from Bows and Spears to Bows and Hammers.

Rhythm Command “Jump” has been revised.

Jump duration shortened from 8 beats to 4 beats.

You can now input rhythm commands while jumping, allowing continuous jumps and switching into attacks or formations.

Camera behavior has been changed.

Players can now manually move the camera left and right, improving visibility and control during combat. Zoom in/out remains available as before.

Hustle Skill 2 unlock conditions have been changed.

It is no longer available by default and must now be unlocked via the Quest Board.

Weapon projectile behavior has been adjusted.

Reviewed throwing logic for spears, bows, and bombs to improve stability and consistency.

New Wave Bosses have been added.

Each world now features a variety of new wave bosses, expanding combat variety.

New Teshita units have been added.

These new minions wield different weapons, introducing fresh threats in battle.

Forts now break down in stages.

During battles, forts are gradually destroyed, heightening tension.

Invincibility has been added after Ratatan revival.

After recovering from being knocked out, Ratatan are temporarily invulnerable, making it easier to regroup.


[hr][/hr]

Balance Adjustments
Welcome Mode benefits have been added.

Starting Tokens and Extra Starting Chorus have been introduced, allowing you to progress more easily from the beginning.

Rhythm Command input window has been relaxed.

The input timing window has been extended, making commands easier to perform.

Tension Gauge gain has been adjusted.

Good: 15 → 6

Just: 30 → 12

Barrier cap now scales with Max HP.

The relationship between defense and durability is clearer, making tactical decisions easier.

Unit Skill: Roman Candle has been adjusted.

Number of shots is now fixed at 3, with increased power per shot.

Improved boss hit accuracy, making it easier to strike the intended target.

Normal attacks and Roman Candle bombs now properly land on aerial platforms.

Boss actions and presentations have been adjusted.

Dekadon: Adjusted behavior for backstep, meteor, jump attack, and burning area effects.

Wagoon: Adjusted HP and charge behavior to improve balance in later phases.

Global adjustments have been made to cobun unit types.

Adjusted movement correction speed and WIZ scaling for all Hustle Techs.

Some Hustle Tech 1 & 2 setups have been swapped.

Drop rates for Legendary and Epic weapons have been increased.

Rare weapons are easier to obtain, improving the growth tempo.

Legendary weapon Decorune effects have been rebalanced.

Effect contents have been streamlined for better overall combat balance.

Rewards and meta-loop distribution across worlds have been optimized.

Growth now feels more natural in line with progression.

Enemy placement, platforms, and backgrounds across worlds have been revised.

Combat rhythm and stage visibility have been improved.

Weather appearance rates have been adjusted.

Reduced bias in occurrences, stabilizing variation in play experience.

Healing Springs now restore MP, and shop healing items now recover minions as well.

Wiz has been removed from Ratatan stats.

Initial cobun count for all unit types has been changed to 4.

A visual effect now triggers when obtaining a Barrier.
Stage, Enemy, and Boss Adjustments
Enemy parameters have been rebalanced overall.

Adjusted HP values for all enemies.

Adjusted collision size and sound effects for turret impacts.

Delayed attack timing for Spear Chief and reduced its damage.

Adjusted spawn rates and placements of wave bosses, and added many new ones.

World 1 adjustments

Adjusted volume of boss BGM.

Added a new enemy: Clamerl.

Adjusted attack timing of Bonbobon.

World 2 adjustments

Removed knockback effect on aerial shots from Kit Lasso.

Updated background layers (foreground/midground) to improve visibility during play.

Adjusted terrain holes so midground seams are no longer visible.

Added a spawn marker for Wagoon.

Adjusted Wagoon’s HP.

Adjustments from World 3 onward

Reviewed HP, attack power, and behavior patterns of various native creatures.

Redesigned wave and platform placements to improve combat flow.

In Worlds 4 and 5, new native fauna wave bosses, Kashira, and Boneless Bear have been added.

Tutorial adjustments

Adjusted Dekadon appearance in the tutorial.

Simplified its behavior and lowered difficulty, making it easier for beginners to clear.

Other adjustments

Adjusted auto-move speed when passing through a Goodie Gate.

Wave bosses now drop special materials.

These materials can be used to craft special weapons distinct from regular ones.
Ratakaruta, Status Abnormalities, and Elemental Force
Ratakaruta rarity rates have been adjusted:

Common: 66% → 55%

Rare: 30% → 36%

Epic: 3% → 6%

Legend: 1% → 3%

New effects have been added to Ratakaruta.

Effect descriptions have been revised to accurately match actual values.

Status ailment adjustments:

Poison: Damage received increase now scales by level (25% / 30% / 35% / 40%).

Burn: Damage dealt reduction effect strengthened (5% → 15%).

Freeze: Duration reduced (8s → 6s), enemy resistance increased.

Shock: Increased additional damage on expiration.

Attribute RataCards / Elemental Force adjustments:

Fire

Burning Blast+ / Hustle Blast+: 7.5%+1% / 15%+2% / 22.5%+3% / 30%+4% → 15%+3% / 25%+6% / 35%+9% / 45%+12%

Burning Bulwhark: 20% / 40% / 60% / 80% → 10% / 20% / 30% / 50%

Burning Boost: 1% / 2% per second → 3% / 5% every 2 seconds

Big Booms: Expanded range, knockback added to explosion

Sacrificial Valor: Duration 10s → 30s

Blaze Ball: Expanded rotation radius

Water

Soaking Splash+ / Hustle Splash+: 36% / 54% / 72% / 90% → 25% / 40% / 55% / 70%

Splash Barrier: 40 / 60 / 80 → 20 / 30 / 40

Splash Initiative: 25% / 50% / 75% / 100% → 10% / 20% / 30% / 50%

Oasis Power: 5% / 10% / 15% → 5% / 7% / 10%

Supreme Soaker: 50% / 100% / 150% / 200% → 30% / 60% / 90% / 120%

Whirlpool Shield: Increase 3 / 5 / 8 → 2 / 3 / 5 (scales with Max HP, reduced barrier cap)

Ice

Grand Finale: Heal conditions 75% / 60% / 50% / 40% → 75% / 60% / 50%

Glacial Heal: 30 / 60 / 100 → 30 / 45 / 60

Frigid Rush: 25% / 50% / 75% / 100% → 15% / 25% / 35% / 50%

Frigid Fury: 30% / 50% → 75% / 100%

Macho Minuet: 20 / 30 → 10 / 15

Cold Shoulder: Now inflicts additional damage on hit

Poison

Poison Drop+: 50% / 100% → 50% (new step) / 100% / 200%

Toxic Boost: 50% / 70% → 75% / 100% (lower proc rate, stronger effect)

Toxic Miasma: 10s → 4s (spec change: Rare tier removed, now inflicts poison level based on rarity)

Lightning

Amped-up Zapper: 6s → 8s

Wizardly Walts: Effect values adjusted (3 / 5 → new settings)

Thunder Freebie: 25% / 35% / 50% → 15% / 33% / 50%

Bolt Boomer+: 25% / 50% → 50% / 100%

Thunder Recovery: 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 → 1 / 2 / 3 / 5

Wind

Whirlwind Strike+ / Hustle Strike+: 25% / 35% / 45% / 60% → 40% / 50% / 60% / 70%

Boss Buster: Effect values adjusted

Hurricane Havoc: 20% / 30% / 50% → 50% / 75% / 100%

Hurricane Combo: 10% / 20% / 40% → 60% / 90% / 120%

Cha-ching Critical: 2 / 5 / 10 → 5 / 7 / 10

Whirlwind Tornado: Damage adjusted


[hr][/hr]

Meta Game
New system: Goddess Games have been added.

An NPC now appears at Rataport, where you can take oaths to adjust difficulty and earn weapon limit-break materials.

Weapon growth EXP requirements have been relaxed.

The amount needed has been reduced, making it easier to raise more weapons.

Weapon crafting material requirements have been reduced.

 Item consumption burden is lighter, allowing for parallel growth of multiple weapons.

Ratatan Quests have been added to the Quest Board.

These can be accepted and progressed from your base, with rewards and goals to support your play cycle.

New upgrade options have been added to the Ratatan Dock.

Growth routes have been expanded in stages, giving you more options for development at Rataport.

New support options have been added to the Support Desk.

This expands pre-battle preparation and upgrade choices.

Movement speed in Rataport has been increased.

Travel time within the base has been shortened, reducing downtime between upgrading, crafting, and deployment.

Newly unlocked items now display a “!” marker.

This prevents overlooked unlocks and makes it immediately clear what to do next.

You can now obtain minions from the Quest Board.

This expands your available squad at deployment, increasing team composition variety.

Help system has been implemented.

Accessible from Rataport, it allows you to check key points of controls and systems.

Ratatan Dock UI has been updated (replacing Nyandola in the lower-left with Baba).

Upgrade unlock timing and costs have been revised overall.

Progression curves have been readjusted to match game pace, easing bottlenecks in early to mid-game.

Unlock timing for features like crafting have been pulled forward to help soften overall difficulty.


[hr][/hr]

UI/UX
Adjusted the layout of the formation screen.

Changed the first-view focus to Cobun, improving the visibility of buttons and various guides.

Revamped the formation screen.

When switching Cobun of the same unit type, stat differences are now displayed in color (blue/red).

If no Decorune is equipped, the details button is now hidden (same behavior applied in the Cobun selection screen).

In the equipment selection and Cobun selection screens, Cobun can now be switched with the L/R buttons without having to return to a higher layer.

Revamped the crafting screen.

In the weapon level-up screen, currently equipped items can now be unequipped via a specific operation and selected as materials.

LB/RB button prompts are now displayed larger.

Operation prompts at the bottom of the screen are now displayed larger.

Required material counts are now displayed larger.

Added a final confirmation dialog when crafting, limit breaking, or leveling up weapons. This prevents accidentally using necessary weapons as materials.

Revamped the Ratakaruta information display screen.

It now clearly shows whether an acquired Ratakaruta is newly obtained or a replacement.

Owned Ratakaruta and Elemental Force effects can now be viewed in a list.

Added an in-game operation guide for the Ratakaruta info screen, making it easier to check effects and controls even during battle.

Expanded the Options menu:

Swap confirm key

Toggle HP gauge and damage numbers ON/OFF

Toggle permanent token display ON/OFF

Adjust character status display position

Select controller icon

Added initial setup options:

On first startup: only language selection is shown.

On first play: Welcome Mode and rhythm input method tutorial/selection dialog is displayed.

Added a result screen.

Reorganized UI and text, and added a treasure chest opening animation with a dedicated sound effect.

Added a shortcut button to Crafting in Rataport.

Adjusted the appearance of the formation, inventory, pause, and help buttons.

Improved boss HP display.

Adjusted gauge size and color, and unified HP bar labeling for wave bosses and other bosses to correct English names.

Implemented a message window.

Conversations and explanations during gameplay can now be displayed in a window format.

Refreshed the title screen.

Redesigned visuals, and Feedback Form text is now displayed.

Adjusted character status display.

Changed the design of speech bubbles.

Improved in-game visibility:

Adjusted Fever effects

Adjusted screen contrast

Adjusted distant background blur effect

Improved overall effects

Revised visuals during bad weather.

Adjusted outlines of native creatures.

Adjusted display fonts (Chinese font updated).


[hr][/hr]

Sound and Voice
Migrated the BGM system to CRIADX.

Optimized volume and playback control.

Calibration adjustment can now be performed from Options > Sound Settings, and it is recommended to re-run the overall calibration.

Replaced all in-game BGM with the latest sound sources.

Updated both in-game and non-game tracks as well as jingles, strengthening overall consistency.

Updated the selectors for WIN/game over jingles and each boss BGM.

Performance effects now transition more naturally according to gameplay situations.

Added and adjusted various sound effects (SE).

Significant improvements made to system operation sounds, player action sounds, and enemy attack sounds.

New SE have been implemented for squad skills, Ratacarta (such as the Water category), and enemy-specific actions.

Implemented NPC voices.

Voice has been added to conversations at the base and during battles, enhancing immersion in the world.

Added unique responses.

Expanded dedicated voice lines and reactions that play in response to player actions.

Added new results screen music.

The results screen after a run now concludes with a more vibrant presentation.

Adjusted various performance effects.

Updated existing effects, improving overall visibility.

Adjusted BGM control.

Improved fade-in/out and loop accuracy in specific scenes.


[hr][/hr]

System, Network, and Optimization
Improved multiplayer connection stability.

Enhanced stability of TLS communication with AWS, and adjusted telemetry transmission data and frequency.

Improved accuracy of random matchmaking.

Added a system to send player country information to the server, enabling more appropriate matchmaking.

Fixed a wide range of online-related exceptions, improving overall stability.

Extended gate waiting time.

Adjusted so that progress remains smooth even if some players have slow connections.

Optimized demos and progression processing before and after match start.

Balanced presentation and loading to prevent progression from halting.

Added host transfer handling.

Multiplayer sessions now continue even if the host disconnects.

Added a reporting feature as an anti-cheat measure.

Players can directly report detected misconduct.

Acquired NAT type and display an announcement if matchmaking is impossible due to NAT restrictions.

Optimized loading times.

Changed to load only necessary data, reducing load times.

Optimized rendering performance.

Reduced workload of various rendering tasks, including effects, and capped frame rate at 240Hz when VSync is disabled.

Reviewed texture resolution and compression for Worlds 4/5 and new variant bosses; atlas creation reduces RAM/VRAM usage and draw calls.

Adjusted background and distant scenery rendering.

Stopped Y-axis scrolling in the background to improve visibility.

Reviewed depth settings for certain effects and optimized stage haze effects.

Refactored internal processing.

Organized Jolly Hermit-related internal code, improving stability.

Localized startup messages for all languages.

Updated Unity to version 6.

Engine migration provides overall optimization and improves future scalability.


[hr][/hr]

Bug Fixes

Battles
Enemy-Related Fixes

Fixed an issue where attack behavior would become erratic under certain conditions.

Fixed an issue where Toxic Curse and Slow Thaw did not affect native creatures.

Resolved a bug where Jolly Hermit’s triple cannon attack animation would break.

Fixed an issue with Bow Chief’s poison mist effect.

Fixed a bug where Cobun hit by Squidly Pete’s ink bomb immediately after a phase clear would stop following and block progress.

Fixed an issue where Squidly Pete would get stuck near walls.

Fixed a rendering issue with Lumabat’s effects.

Fixed a mismatch in hit detection during transformation of W3 Lord Rosham Bo.

Corrected the attack effect display for Shield Chief.

Fixed an issue where Jolly Hermit’s water beam attack effect would cut off midway.

Fixed a bug where multiple hitboxes hitting a single enemy at the same time would incorrectly stack all damage.
Battle System
Fixed a bug where critical damage multipliers were higher than intended.

Fixed various Cobun control and behavior bugs.

Fixed an issue with the Splash Combo.

Fixed a bug where tornado movement speed differed from intended values (standardized the time basis used for distance calculation).

Fixed regressions in target detection.

Fixed an issue where target acquisition would fail during attack states.

Fixed marker display issues for Spear Chief/Bow Chief wave bosses.

Fixed an issue where long-press jump could not control jump strength.

Fixed incorrect attack hit registration for Pike Cobun.

Fixed an issue where the Zap Bonus (Legendary) effect was not applied.

Fixed a bug where knockback did not occur with Impact Lance (adjusted so native creatures are knocked back properly).

Fixed a bug where Cobun animations could freeze or become unresponsive on platforms.

Fixed the flight distance issue of Poison Arrow.

Fixed a bug where Decorune’s status effect damage enhancements would stack indefinitely.

Fixed an issue where Ratakaruta buffs did not apply correctly to additional Cobun in the intended order.

Fixed a bug where Amped-Up Zapper effects were not triggered correctly.

Fixed issues with unique Decorune.

Fixed a bug where critical multipliers were calculated lower than intended.

Fixed errors occurring with Happy Decorune.

Fixed issues with Ratakaruta implementation related to water splash effects.

Fixed Fantasy Decorune issues.

Fixed a bug where Poison category effects triggered every command.

Fixed a bug where Wind category effects triggered every command.

Fixed an issue where changing the rhythm command type in-game disabled Hustle Tech 2.

Fixed issues with Bitter Chill+/Hustle Chill+ not applying effects correctly.

Fixed buff parameter specification errors in Frigid Rush.

Fixed unnatural gaps between the first and second shots of bow attacks.

Fixed a bug where category effect quantity limits were not functioning correctly.

Fixed an issue where Cobun alignment did not work properly.
Multiplayer
Fixed an issue where communication would cross between worlds.

Fixed some issues where host behavior would cause inconsistent gameplay in multiplayer.

Fixed a bug where dying almost simultaneously with a player under From the Brink in multiplayer could trigger a game over.

Fixed exceptions that occurred when a session was disconnected.

Fixed exceptions that could occur when transitioning from the lobby.

Fixed a bug where leaving a session while an ice Ratakaruta effect was active in online multiplayer would cause an error.

Fixed a bug where selecting multiplayer for the first time could cause an error if a scene transition occurred while the lobby popup help was displayed.

Fixed exceptions caused by incorrect disposal control when changing the session owner.

Fixed a bug where fade-in timing was misaligned at the start of multiplayer battles.

Fixed a bug where progress would halt if the room owner disconnected while waiting.

Fixed timing misalignment when starting multiplayer games.

Fixed incorrect state transitions when switching Ratatan → COMtan on disconnection, mainly during Interval phases.

Fixed a bug where a game over would trigger if a player died while another player’s From the Brink reached 0.
Other
Fixed a bug where objects generated when enemies are hit would appear offset from the attack hit position.

Fixed a bug where the screen would glitch if the Ratatan was knocked back while zoomed in.

Fixed a bug where the Ratatan would get stuck when jumping to the edge of a platform.

Fixed a bug where the in-game Ratakaruta display button did not switch to keyboard mode.

Fixed Cobun gauge UI showing MAX incorrectly (0/0 no longer displays MAX; gauge hidden when no Cobun are present).

Fixed an issue where the rhythm gauge display could be inverted.

Fixed a bug where the number of wind Ratakaruta was not counted in in-game info display.

Fixed a bug where characters would not return fully to the wall after clipping into it.

Fixed an error occurring after Ratakaruta selection.

Fixed various flickering issues of allied characters (Cobun).

Fixed handling of offset values for Cobun alignment.

Partially fixed a bug where elapsed time during pause would jump forward abruptly when unpausing.

Fixed an issue where save data could not be deleted.

Fixed a bug where leaving the game in-game could cause an error.

Fixed a bug where starting a new game could inherit weapons from the previous slot.

Fixed a bug where item drop trails would not disappear.

Partially fixed an issue where enemies could be knocked beyond gates.

Fixed a bug where data interrupted in the first wave would not be restored.

Fixed a bug where HP gauges of Cobun who joined late would not display correctly.

Fixed a bug in the in-game character status display at the top-left corner.

Fixed a bug where Cobun could be prevented from passing through gates if residual attack effects caused burn/freeze immediately after phase clear.
World
Fixed a bug where recovery item descriptions in the in-game shop were not displayed correctly.

Fixed lobby demo behavior so that interrupted demos are correctly marked as “completed.”

Fixed a bug where progress would halt if a 3-player party chose different Goodie Gates.

Fixed a bug in World 2 where the gate to the next wave would sometimes not appear.

Fixed a bug where the camera state from the previous world carried over after switching worlds.

Fixed a bug where camera position would be offset at the start of a world.

Fixed a bug where the top-right menu icon appeared during lobby demo playback.

Fixed a bug where some players could not pass through Goodie Gates even when opened.

Fixed a bug where the farthest in-game background could be cut off.

Fixed a bug where certain demos would not play in the lobby under specific conditions.

Fixed a bug where item drop lists were not set when entering the same world consecutively.

Fixed a bug where weapons and items could disappear when closing the application.
Tutorial
Fixed a bug where the font did not switch in popup help.

Fixed a bug where text overlapped in the tutorial demo under certain language settings.

Fixed an issue where BGM would not resume after unpausing at the beginning of the tutorial.

Fixed a bug where the tutorial could not progress when the rhythm command input mode was set to Advanced.

Fixed a bug where the tutorial would freeze in Traditional Chinese / Simplified Chinese environments.

Fixed a bug where, after obtaining instruments in the tutorial, Just timing effects played while the music score remained hidden.

Fixed a bug where tutorial BGM continued playing on the title screen after returning from the tutorial.
Meta Game
Fixed a bug where controls became unresponsive after changing the language in options.

Fixed a bug where Donut Love and Candy Love effects did not apply correctly.

Fixed a bug where some characters would stop acting properly after opening and closing the pause menu.

Fixed a bug on the title screen where the cursor appeared to jump unexpectedly.

Fixed a bug where changing sort order on the quest board, then switching tabs, could halt progress.

Fixed a bug where items would duplicate across slots.

Fixed a bug where items would not persist correctly.

Corrected effect settings in the Ratatan Dock.

Fixed various issues related to interrupted saves.

Fixed a bug where cursor initial positions were incorrect in language selection, Cobun selection, and weapon selection screens.

Fixed layout issues for character status in the top-left of Rataport.

Fixed a bug where Decorune names were cut off in some languages.

Fixed incorrect thumbnail images for Worlds 1 and 3 on the save screen.

Fixed a bug where the Feedback Form text on the title screen was not displayed.
Sound
Fixed SE playback for selecting slots in online save data when the tutorial has not been completed.

Fixed various BGM playback issues.

Fixed a bug where incorrect SE would play during lightning strikes.

Fixed SE playback for cannon projectile impacts.

Corrected Ratatan voice pronunciation.

Fixed SE playback when using advance input mode.

Fixed SE for Cobun voice lines not playing correctly when all Cobun are defeated.

Fixed SE not playing in certain dialogues.

Fixed a bug where, if a single melody rank persisted for a long time within one phase, character actions would go out of sync with the music rhythm.
Known Issues
These are currently known issues. They are either scheduled to be addressed in upcoming patches, or investigations into the causes are currently ongoing.

In multiplayer, player synchronization may occasionally become misaligned.

In multiplayer, after selecting a switch, some players’ doors may not open, preventing progress.

In multiplayer, certain demo scenes may display other players’ animations incorrectly.

In multiplayer, if a lobby once reaches full capacity with 4 players, then the number drops to 3 or fewer, new players may no longer be able to join.

This can be resolved by leaving the lobby and creating a new one.

In multiplayer, a match may occur with a lobby where players have already deployed.

Progress can resume when the last player to enter the lobby leaves.

In some languages, text on the altar may be cut off.

In some languages, certain characters may not display.

Effect description text for player upgrades From the Brink and Never Surrender does not match the actual effects.

notes.title: Patapon spiritual successor Ratatan musically marches towards an early access release next month
notes.notes:
If we're being honest with ourselves, the original PSP was a sort of Proto-Switch too, no? As in it was home to a lot of odd, smaller-scope games that not many other platforms might have featured outside of Nintendo's earlier handhelds. Patapon was one such tiny oddity, one of the most charming games on the platform, if not to ever outright exist. It did go on to get a couple of sequels, but the series (outside of an upcoming remaster of the first two) is sort of dead. Luckily, Ratatan, a spiritual successor from Patapon's creator is here to satisfy your tiny-guy-chanting-to-music needs with a newly revealed release date!

 Read more

notes.title: Update #5
notes.notes:
Hello RataTEAM! 

First off thanks for the great feedback on the backer Beta. It's been invaluable for providing insight in areas we can focus on for improvement. Also, for those of you who didn't get a chance to play the Beta, we are cooking something up to allow more people the chance to play in the near future now that we have given precedence to our backers.

It's been over a year and a half since we launched our Ratatan Kickstarter campaign so we are going to slow down the frequency of updates. We have completed the closed Beta and are getting closer and closer to a release so we want to keep a few surprises up our sleeves. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312450/f608f2bc2139971f312cd92c10fbf22af2ab022d.png
Developer Update 

Scheduled Dates Listed in the Kickstarter Campaign
To everyone who has supported Ratatan, we can't thank you enough for your warm and continued support.

We apologize for the lack of explanation on our part regarding the Kickstarter delivery date being listed as April 2025. This led to a situation where that date was mistaken for a final release date. This date ws an estimate of when we expected to deliver rewards to our backers, but is not the official release date.

We are working diligently to prepare an official launch date for Ratatan and will make a clear announcement once a decision has been made.

We apologize for any inconvenience this has caused and will continue to make every effort to meet your expectations. Thank you for your continued support!
 
Ongoing Milestones 
Now that the Closed Beta Test is over, the next step is to prepare for the open beta and early access. At this point, many issues still remain. Many have enjoyed the game, but there have also been some concerns and anxieties.
The development team will continue to address these issues and expand upon the game's content in preparation for the next milestone. We will also continue to add polish and new content even after early access. I'll explain our roadmap when the time comes.
Please know, we will continue to develop the game with the aim of making it a GOTY award-winning title.
Thank you all for your continued support of Ratatan.
Producer Kazuto Sakajiri

Introduction

notes.title: Update #4
notes.notes:
Hello RataTEAM! 

It's update time and of course we have more information about the ongoing backer beta. It's a big update so grab a seat and have a read! 

MIX Spring Showcase
Ratatan will be taking part in The MIX Spring Showcase on March 17th during GDC week. The showcase is a digital event featuring news, reveals, announcements and more. The show kicks off at 9:00AM Pacific Time and can be viewed on the following channels:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312450/a2b3781b37f00a9b779cce2c580cfb653fece7fd.png
YouTube / Twitch / Homepage

Development Update
In this update, we're going to go over the Closed Beta Test that is currently underway and how it is progressing.

The main features of this supersized update will be the addition of World 2's Yeehawler Mountain and its boss the Wagoon, as well as the next Ratatan, Kamonelo and the new Wand wielding cobun.

Bad Day on Yeehawler Mountain
Deep in the dry, windswept wilderness, a rail car once carried gilded treasures through the canyon. But now it's up to you to infiltrate Yeehawler Ranch, home of the roaming Wagoon, and seize its owner, Saguaro Slim!

This area's boss, Wagoon, will call out to the female Bessoons to help him when he's under attack, and has a habit of diving into the sand to attack you from below!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312450/ab423b09468518fc977e11eb91fa9dd0fad8b6ab.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312450/29cea930ad2c2faa2cc5de56af82c533afb79b83.png

Kamonelo
Character Introduction
Kamonelo (VA: Nonoka Obuchi)

Behind Kamonelo's blank expression, is a mind operating at speeds we can only imagine, pondering the world's complexities.
They’ll sometimes overthink and act in ways that are incomprehensible.
They enjoy looking at the sky.
"To fly or not to fly, that is likely the question."
"Oh, to be nice and empty, like the sky..."

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312450/7aa6bbd93113228ce029bd97d31b6baf7ba4027b.jpg
Magical Cobun
Kamonelo’s cobun.
Proficient with a wand.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312450/029685f4bb098caafc853a136405413b4a627743.png

We have already received a lot of feedback from the Closed Beta test identifying many glitches and parts of the game with low useability. It's difficult to respond to all of these issues right away, so we're examining them one by one and will update the game to make it even better.
Please refer to the patch notes below for more details on this update.

Closed Beta v0.2.67 Patch Notes

Highlights

 World 2: Bad Day on Yeehawler Mountain is now available.
The boss, Wagoon, has a distinctive attack, such as summoning Bessoons to increase its attack capacity or diving into the sand to attack from below.
Once the Wagoon is defeated, the game can then be played in a circular fashion. 
 Added Kamonelo functionality to Ratatan
This Ratatan initially enters fights with Assault Cobun and Magical Cobun. The cobun's HP is restored slightly when the rhythm command gathers everyone together, so the troops can last longer if this cobun is utilized effectively.
 Added the wand cobun class.
A long-range weapon, the wand's means of attack changes depending on the attributes of any implemented Ratakaruta.
The unit skill allows them to target enemies and gather in one place, or target an ally to boost their attack power.


Battle

 It is now possible to input a rhythm command and move the Ratatan except while taking a performance motion.
An occurrence where the Ratatan was unable to act more than expected when failing a rhythm command input, etc., has been resolved.
 The maximum number of cobun that can join an adventure has been changed from 6 to 9.
The maximum number of cobun will be expandable at the support desk in the future.
The number of cobun that can be taken by default is currently set in the player enhancement menu, but will be further expanded in the future.
 When a cobun is caught by a monster or some other obstacle during the “Align” rhythm command, it will now slip through and return to the vicinity of the Ratatan.
 The following enemy long-range attacks now display a marker on the target of the attack:
Pointy Chief / Pinchy

Balance Adjustments

 Adjusted the HP, attack power, and action interval of Teshita or other enemies.
 The arrows fired by Teshita's bow attacks have been made more visible.
 The damage of the Jolly Hermit's great move Frenzied Fish Cannon has been adjusted.
 The damage reduction percentage during the effects of the rhythm command "Guard" has been increased. Also, while under the effect of Guard, the player will no longer be knocked back even if hit by an attack that would typically do so.

 
Meta Gameplay

 We have adjusted the amount of experience gained per material when leveling up weapons through crafting.
The amount of experience gained at level 1 has been adjusted, making it easier to level up overall.
 We've removed boss materials from the Exchanger that were registered as items that could be exchanged for general-purpose material and other items.
 Boss materials are dropped when a boss is defeated (there are multiple drops, one of which is dropped at random), and weapons that can be crafted using those materials also have a low probability of dropping when that same boss is defeated.
 What will happen when using the "Skill 1" and "Skill 2" rhythm commands can now be confirmed on the composition screen.
 The functions and how they are represented in the Craft Menu, Inventory, and Organization screens have been unified, such as those for equipped and the item lock function.
 Added text to the call icons on the inventory, organization screen, and pause menu to indicate which menus can be called.
 After the appearance of NPCs at the Support Desk, My Room, Exchanger, and Crafting, will now only describe their facilities the first time you interact with them.


Other

 The fourth beat in the line indicating beats in the rhythm gauge has been removed.
 The Rhythm Command Guide is now displayed when adventuring.
The display can be turned on or off in the options.
 Added explanation text for items and choruses that can be acquired during an adventure.
 Changed the cobun response voice when failing a rhythm command.
 

Bugfixes

 Fixed a bug where Hermit's great move Frenzied Fish Cannon was sometimes triggered at a time where it could not be dodged by the rhythm command.
 Fixed a bug in which some tutorials would not play when starting the game again after being interrupted.
 Fixed a bug where the attack detection in World 1's Squiddly Pete was set to something unexpected.
 Fixed a bug where weapon leveling in crafting was not behaving properly.
 Fixed a bug where weapon levels were not displayed correctly in the sortie screen.
 Fixed a bug where the appearance of one weapon was replacing the appearance of another weapon during certain movements.
 Fixed a bug where certain event progress flags wouldn't appear, making progression impossible when obtaining a cobun early at certain points in the tutorial.
 Fixed a bug in which game progression stops when two or more players increase the number of cobun in a multiplayer game using the enhancement item Arms Expansion (used to increase the initial number of cobun that can be taken on an adventure).


Known Issues

 A bug where your Ratatan and cobun would get stuck in the Goodie Gate after being hit by an attack that causes them to blow up in battle has been temporarily addressed and corrected to prevent it from occurring.
However, we will need more time to correct the bug so that it no longer occurs at all.
 There are other minor problems with the display of text within speech bubbles:
Immediately after a facility is opened, the facility NPC will talk about that facility, but this text may not be displayed correctly.
Lines for World 1 may appear in World 2.

notes.title: Update #3
notes.notes:
Hello! Producer Sakajiri, here.
Thank you all for your patience!
This month we'd like to share some details about the long-awaited closed beta test.

Wishlists Now Exceed 100,000!
Thanks to your tremendous support, the number of wishlists on our Steam page is now more than 100,000! Thank you so much.
We've also received over 100 ratings for the Ratatan Original Soundtrack Demo, all of which have been positive. This is super encouraging for everyone on the department team, and we are working hard every day to create something that meets and hopefully exceeds your expectations.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312450/f93357e3d1d385b7af65b38c1a322514e742ee03.jpg

- About the Date for Closed Beta Test
Provided we don't hit any major obstacles, the Beta is scheduled to start on February 27, 2025. The distribution of codes, start date, and time will be announced via Discord and X as soon as they are confirmed.

However, we have sadly decided to forego the upcoming Steam Next Fest. Instead, we have made the decision to prioritize the closed beta test, and plan to better prepare a demo that will be available to the general public at the next Steam Next festival in June.

We look forward to your continued support and encouragement as we continue to develop this project ahead of a major rollout that will come in the summer.

- Beta Test Overview
When the closed beta test is released, up to the end of Stage 1 is planned to be playable in the initial build. The test period is expected to last roughly one month with multiple updates throughout, including the addition of Stages 2 and 3 and more Ratatan, as well as extra features.

We will also provide a survey form during the test, so please feel free to give us your honest opinions and suggestions so that we can improve the quality of the game. We have reviewed all the feedback we have received so far and incorporated it into our plans, but it can take a long time before that feedback is reflected. We appreciate your understanding.

- Items for Consideration
We have received many opinions and suggestions regarding command inputs. Rest assured, the team is aware of these and is considering them.
In addition to these, we'd like for players to do things like switch button combinations and show/hide guides in the options menu. We are preparing to test this as much as possible during the closed beta.

- Test Precautions

 We ask that you please participate in the beta with courtesy and within our guidelines.
 Many glitches will be present due to the nature of the beta build. Please be aware that these may impede your ability to play the game.
 There is still a possibility of mis-synchronization and connection problems when it comes to multiplayer.
 Communication data from this test will be collected to improve the multiplayer experience.

- Requests
Due to the postponement of participation in the Steam Next Fest, we ask that participants please refrain from taking screenshots and videos of the game, and distributing them or posting them on social media. However, you may share the information in the official Ratatan Discord. If you are a member of the media or a distributor, then please contact our management.

Development Update
Welcome to the February development update!
We hope you're excited for the closed beta at the end of the month, so we're gonna show you a little bit of new information.

Not only will there be general matchmaking, but matching with friends will also be available!

The closed beta will also include a tutorial at the start of the game--something that was requested in the feedback. Finally, you'll be able to meet Crow in game!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312450/a3f88cc26613f4845270309ca20c226c5c377f1c.png

Not only that, but instant enhancement items have been added and adjusted. We hope you're looking forward to trying these for yourselves!

notes.title: Update #2
notes.notes:
Campaign Update

■ About the Closed Beta
We are currently preparing for the beta's implementation in February as planned, however, while this is the current plan, the final announcement will be in the next update.

Eligibility:
Any backer who has backed the base digital or physical tier or higher via Kickstarter or Backerkit.

Duration:
From mid-February to the end of March

How to Participate:
We will send your Steam Beta Download Key to your registered Kickstarter or Backerkit E-mail address. There may be some unforeseen delays due to the large number of keys required, however we will do our best to deliver everyone’s Beta key together on the same day.

We will continue to support customer service requests via the official Ratatan Discord and support E-mail address. When sending in a support request, please provide your backer number and registered E-mail address with it so we can confirm your details and expedite the process. 

About the Test:

 Stages 1 to 3 are planned to be playable in the beta test.
 The game is still under development, so there may be bugs and tentative features.
 There will be no restrictions with sharing footage or screenshots. However, we would appreciate it if you could be considerate of the many bugs and tentative features that may appear in the game.
 Any save data from the alpha test will not carry over into the beta test. We will also do our best not to reset saved data during the beta test, but this may become necessary in some cases.
 Please be aware that there will be roughly 20,000 participants in this next test, which is a considerable number. We ask that all participants please enjoy the game online while being considerate of others.

■ About Steam Next Fest
We will be releasing a demo version of the game to be exhibited during the Steam Next Fest in February.
The content of the demo version will be limited to only Stage 1.
Online play will be available, but players will not be able to match with participants in the closed beta test that will be running in parallel.

■ Taipei Game Show 2025
Ratatan will be exhibiting at the Taipei Game Show being held from January 23 to January 26, and we'll post updates on how that's going via our social media!
https://tgs.tca.org.tw/index_e.php


Development Update
Happy New Year, everyone! (Akemashite omedetou gozaimasu!)
We'll be unveiling some of the elements that are currently being implemented, including those that we mentioned previously. We hope you're excited!

■ New Additions: Kamonelo and the Magical Cobun
After Pyokorappa's addition, Kamonelo, who was briefly shown in the promotional video, finally became a playable character in Ratatan. Kamonelo's trusty sidekick, the staff-wielding Magical Cobun, is also here to play.
The Magical Cobun is an interesting unit that changes the appearance and trajectory of its attacks depending on the Ratakaruta it is holding.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312450/f6e0dfc0ba4804da9fccef646c5c2c07d01cc54c.gif

■ Implementing New Worlds and New Monsters

notes.title: Update #1
notes.notes:
Ongoing Development

First of all, we are pleased to announce the successful completion of the alpha test.
Due to operational reasons, the number of participants for this test was limited to only 500, and it's a shame that not many people were able to participate. We apologize for this.
That said, we would like to report on the details of the test in the development update to follow.

As for future plans, the development team is currently preparing for beta testing.
If all goes well, the test will be conducted in February of 2025 and will be open to all beta access holders. The scope of the test will be expanded from the alpha, and we expect players to be able to experience up to Stage 3 of Ratatan.

We also hope to take part in the Steam Next Fest in February, 2025 as well, however it will require a demo in order to participate, so we need to figure out how to separate that from the beta test.

We'd love it if you could help us know how best to strike that balance between fulfilling your rights as a backer and the development of the title altogether.
Ratatan has only received this opportunity because of all your support, and our respect for our backers will never change.
Thank you for your continued support.

Development Update
Introduction
This is a report on the alpha test we conducted in November.
This test was limited to a maximum of 500 people.
The alpha ROM was tested with many glitches in multiplayer and other areas, and we believe that there were many areas where players could not enjoy the game properly. However, we were able to get a lot of responses through our survey. Thank you all very much for your help!

Survey Results
The survey was obtained in the same format as the Steam store.

Results:
122/127 (96% favorable)

Since the test participants consisted only of backers, we fully understand that favorable result might be a little biased, but we feel very encouraged that so many of you were able to recognize our hard work. As mentioned earlier, there are still a number of glitches and areas that have not been adjusted properly, which has shown us again that we must tighten our focus in our development efforts.

Feedback from Test Participants and Response Guidelines
We have identified several issues by analyzing the many comments we received. We have determined that not all of them require major adjustments, but simply a bit of polish. The following three major guidelines are used to guide our response to these issues:

[olist]
 Remove inconveniences and absurdities
 Remove incomprehensibility
 Improve the rhythm command experience
[/olist]

Remove Inconveniences and Absurdities
The game was lacking in areas that were mainly caused by development reasons, and we're considering adjusting the following issues:


 Hermit's beam attack and other big moves have been adjusted so that they are made in time with the rhythm.
 Relax the rigidity of the rhythm command inputs.
 When a rhythm command fails, make it possible to input the rhythm command from the next musical bar.
 In the craft menu, implement a function to disassemble weapons and convert them into material items that can be used for crafting.


Remove Incomprehensibility
While we believe that a small tutorial is necessary, we intend to design the game so it can be played without a tutorial or explanation.


 Reorganize the in-game UI to show if troop skills can be used in relation to the amount of MP remaining.
 Adjust the in-game store so that an item's effect can be checked when hovering over it.
 Review the response when a Ratatan is attacked.
 Add wording to the description of material items in the inventory to indicate what they are used for.
 Display the type and quantity of material items required for each item in the player enhancement menu, support desk menu, and crafting menu.
 Add a guide highlighting interactable objects, items, and NPCs when approaching them at certain distances, etc.
 

Improve the Rhythm Command Experience
As a guideline for play after the beta, we would like to make it possible to realize various play styles by combining Ratatan x Cobun (weapon type) x Rhythm Command.

First of all, we are planning to give unique abilities (i.e. Ratatan abilities) for each Ratatan.

[olist]
 Abilities that enhance the effect of specific rhythm commands.
 Abilities that provide a bonus for successful rhythm input, such as just-in-time inputs.
 Those that give permanent abilities, etc..
[/olist]

In this way, the abilities will vary from Ratatan to Ratatan. This is how we intend to individualize the play style of each Ratatan in the game.

Next, for Cobun, we will add specific effects to troop skills, such as making it easier to destroy forts and such, or to blow up enemies and cancel their actions, as a means of differentiating between vanguard, mid-guard, and rear-guard troop types. We would like to make changing troop types and skills more meaningful in terms of gameplay than we have before.

Finally, for the rhythm commands, organizing what each command does and clarifying its role will make the effect of including the appropriate rhythm command in each situation more precise.

Taken together, these measures will help to realize the combination of Ratatan and Cobun by correctly judging their play style and inputting rhythm commands. We are planning to implement each of these measures for the beta, and we hope that you will join the rhythm action in the beta version once again.

Now, this is not to say that all of the above will be addressed as described above. We will also be adding content, fixing bugs, and adjusting the matching system in preparation for the beta test.

Although there are only a few days left until the beta test is upon us, the team will do its utmost to deliver an even better experience.

notes.title: RATATAN v0.2.20 Patch Notes
notes.notes:
[UPDATE]

 Pyokorappa can now be selected.
 Assault Cobun can now be selected. (Unlocking via Utility Enhancement will allow them to be used with other Ratatans too.) 
 Lances are now dropped by enemies.
 Phase rewards now rarely yield two or more Cobun.
 The save data screen layout has been adjusted.
 The button design for moving between the sortie and inventory screens in the Rataport has been changed.
 The Ratatan's in-game jump behavior has been adjusted.
 Multiplayer stability has been improved.
 If any player disconnects while in game, everyone will be returned to the title. 
 If an error occurs, it will be displayed on the screen in large red letters. (It would be very much appreciated if you could send a screen shot of the error screen along with the log when you report a bug.)


[BUG FIXES]

 Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when using attack commands.
 Fixed a bug that caused knocked back characters to keep sliding during multiplayer.
 Fixed a bug that caused the mob enemies to leap from side to side while moving.
 Fixed a bug where mob enemies would continue chasing Cobun.
 Fixed a bug that caused the screen display to break when repeatedly pressing the back button while on the sortie screen.
 Fixed a bug that can cause a series of similar terrain or enemy placements.
 Fixed a bug that could cause a crash when returning to the Rataport from a level.
 Fixed a bug that could cause other players in the Rataport to become irresponsive during multiplayer.
 Fixed several bugs related to network synchronization.

[CHARACTER INTRODUCTION]
【Pyokorappa】 (VA: Sally Amaki)
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45312450/192635c30d9b16db92582428f076b55a19618a63.png
Character Traits:

 Sharp-tongued, they have a pretty overbearing attitude toward others.
 But they're actually deeply lonely and care about everyone.
 They often regret their actions and cry their eyes out when they are alone.

Assault Cobun:

 Pyokorappa's Cobun.
 Pretty handy with a lance.

[hr][/hr]
[DIRECTOR'S NOTE]
Something that likely caught your medama in this update is the implementation of the long awaited　Ratatan, Pyokorappa, and the Assault Cobun.
The Assault Cobun is a lance user and the second in the vanguard class, but while it attacks aggressively with its lance from a certain distance, it does not have as high HP as the Soldier Cobun and is vulnerable to being shot.
It's an aggressive class that can keep attacking without taking damage by utilizing the formation command and pulling them back near your Ratatan as needed, so please give it a try.
We are also working on fixing bugs as needed based on the reports we receive. The fixes are being made in order of severity, starting with crashes, freezes, and anything blocking player progress.
Alongside this, we are also working on improving the synchronization of Ratatan's online multiplayer, but this is still in progress. We have confirmed that some problems may occur as a result of a combination of multiple factors, and will likely require a little more time.

notes.title: Update #0
notes.notes:
Hello Ratatan fans!

In case you missed it, Ratatan now has a store page on Steam!
We have finally made it to this point thanks to the tremendous support we received through last year's Kickstarter, and we would like to thank our fans again for all of that support.

We have been informing you of our development progress and will continue these efforts in the same manner going forward. We understand that some of you are new to the Ratatan community, so below is a list of our past updates. Please take a look if you’re interested, but bear in mind there are a lot of them!

Kickstarter Updates:
https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/ratata-arts/ratatan/posts


PROJECT STATUS
Development is currently in the alpha stage and testing is underway. Based on the results of that test, we will move on to developing the beta. Our policy is to work together with our fans in Ratatan's development, including its intermediate stages.

We would like for everyone to try Ratatan as soon as possible in order to gather more feedback and suggestions, and we thank you for your patience as we work towards that.

FUTURE UPDATES
While you're waiting, we will continue to report on the development progress at least once a month. We would like to introduce concept art and skills, propose game ideas, and provide information on events, merchandise, and development of other multimedia.

Ratatan is a project that will continue to move forward together with its fans, and the entire Ratatan development team is feeling encouraged by your kind comments. We will continue to strive to make the game the best it can be, and we hope that you will join us as fellow members of the development team. And finally, don't forget to wishlist Ratatan on Steam!

The Ratatan Dev Team
